office_explainer: Runs county government and emergency response and leads Commissioners Court. Not a courtroom job.
why_it_matters: Open seat: Judge Lina Hidalgo is not running. The county judge leads Harris County's disaster response and Commissioners Court, which voted in September to raise the county property tax rate 7.6%.

candidates.name: Orlando Sanchez
candidates.background: Harris County Treasurer for 12 years; earlier served on Houston City Council.

own_words.text: At an Oct. 1 forum, would not give a yes or no on renewing the county's Flock license-plate camera contract; said the decision should rest on input from citizens and law enforcement, with penalties for policy violations.

candidates.name: Letitia Plummer
candidates.background: Former Houston City Council member who resigned in 2025 under Texas's resign-to-run rule; won the May 2026 Democratic runoff over former Mayor Annise Parker.

own_words.text: At an Oct. 1 forum, said she would not renew the Flock camera contract as written, citing privacy concerns, and wants a public policy on who can see the data and how long it is kept.

candidates.name: Vince Duncan
candidates.background: Declared write-in candidate. Write-in names are not printed on the ballot; you must write the name in.

own_words.text: At an Oct. 1 forum, said he would end the Flock camera contract outright, opposing what he called 24-hour surveillance.

candidates.name: Marianne "Yan" Hess
candidates.background: Declared write-in candidate. Write-in names are not printed on the ballot; you must write the name in.

own_words.text: At an Oct. 1 forum, said she would not renew the Flock camera contract unless privacy, misuse and mistaken-arrest concerns are resolved.
